extracted.intended_audience: law students, patent practitioners, and judges studying or applying novelty/utility principles in patent law
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on legal standards for novelty and prior use in patent law: who counts as a prior user, the relevant timing, distinction between product and process, reduction to practice, abandonment, evidence burdens, and the race-of-diligence rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory novelty requirement (not known or used by others)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject-matter of a patent should not have been 'known or used by others before the discovery or invention thereof' by the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase is construed to mean not known or used by others (i.e., the public or persons other than the patentee) prior to the patentee's discovery; if known or used by others before the patentee's discovery, the patent may be invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant time for prior knowledge/use (US vs England)
rubrics_metrics.description: In England knowledge obtained at any time before the application suffices to invalidate; in the United States the decisive time is before the discovery by the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The U.S. construction confines prior use/knowledge to the period before the patentee's discovery (per the Acts of 1793 and 1836), whereas English law extends to any time before application/issuance and may treat discontinued uses differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'others' — who can invalidate a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'others' denotes some person or persons other than the patentee; prior use by one person other than the patentee is sufficient to show the patentee was not first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not necessary that many people knew or used it — a single other person's prior use can defeat novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use defeats patent; patentee's private use does not
rubrics_metrics.description: Public use or exercise of the invention by others before the patentee's discovery invalidates; private use by the patentee himself prior to application does not necessarily deprive him of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute aims to give the public early benefit; the patentee's own private use (or limited knowledge by him) is not treated as prior public use that defeats his claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: product existence versus knowledge of the process
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere prior existence of a product (produced by a lost or secret process) does not automatically show the prior 'use' or 'knowledge' of the art of making it; for arts/processes the 'thing patented' may be the process, not just the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the prior manufacture existed but the art of making it was lost or unknown, production of a specimen of the product alone may not negative a later inventor's claim to his process of making the thing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of statute to different subject-matters (machine vs art/process)
rubrics_metrics.description: The words of the statute must be applied separately to each subject-matter: art, machine, manufacture, composition, etc.; in machines the product itself often reveals the invention, while in processes the invention consists in the manner of producing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because machines are combinations of parts detectable on inspection, prior existence of the same machine more readily negates novelty; processes may be independently invented even if product appears the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: First inventor requirement — priority in time and perfection
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee must be the 'original and first inventor' in point of time; an invention must be perfected and put into actual use (reduced to practice) to be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An imperfect, incomplete, or merely theoretical invention not reduced to practice is not patentable; priority favors the first to reduce to a fixed, practical form, subject to the reasonable-diligence qualification (see race of diligence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to practice / embodiment required to be a prior invention
rubrics_metrics.description: To constitute a prior invention that defeats a later patent, the earlier party must have proceeded far enough to be entitled to a patent — i.e., reduced the idea to practice and embodied it in some distinct form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conception alone is insufficient; the prior inventor must have carried the idea into practical operation (distinct machinery, apparatus, manufacture, or composition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere trials/experiments do not vitiate a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Mere trials and experiments, even if continued up to the date of a patent, will not vitiate the grant if the patentee had no knowledge of those trials or if the prior acts were only experimental and not completed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts examine whether the prior actor abandoned the pursuit (abandonment presumption) or continued experiments; abandonment supports inference of mere experimentation rather than completed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment as evidence that prior acts were experimental
rubrics_metrics.description: If a prior inventor abandoned the pursuit of the invention, that abandonment furnishes a presumption that his proceedings rested in experiment and trial only, not a completed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long discontinuance or giving up the project (e.g., for decades) strongly suggests lack of completed invention; continuous effort without abandonment makes it a factual question whether the same substantial result was attained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race-of-diligence / priority rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In a race between independent inventors, the one who first reduces the invention to a fixed, positive, and practical form is generally entitled to priority; however, the one who first invents may have prior rights if 'using reasonable diligence' to adapt and perfect the invention (section 15 qualification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority may favor earlier conception if the earlier party is actively and reasonably diligent in bringing the invention to practice; statutory language and cases qualify pure 'first to conceive' by a diligence requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence burden and presumptions — plaintiff rests on patent until overthrown
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee may rest upon his patent as initial evidence of novelty; to defeat it the defendant must prove prior invention or prior public use/description. Courts have instructed that if reasonable doubt exists about priority, the benefit goes to the plaintiff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plaintiff can introduce testimony from persons 'in the way of hearing' to show they had not heard of the invention (exhausting affirmative instances). Defendants bear the burden to show the negative (prior knowledge/use) sufficient to overthrow the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory defenses: prior description in public work or prior public use
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute provides that the thing patented is subject to defence that the patentee was not the original and first inventor or that it had been described in some public work, or had been in public use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof that the invention was previously described in a public work or publicly used before the patentee's invention may invalidate the patent; courts analyze the character, extent, and publicity of such prior disclosure or use.

rubrics_metrics.name: English doctrine on discontinued but not forgotten public use
rubrics_metrics.description: Under English decisions, a prior use of an invention, even if discontinued, will invalidate a subsequent patent if it has been once publicly used and the recollection of it has not been wholly lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This treats prior public use of machinery as negating the proposition that the subsequent patentee was the first inventor; the U.S. approach distinguishes lost/forgotten arts differently.
